screens_reviewed: Single scroll capture of the audit wizard step 1 (Context) on an Android tablet in light theme, showing the place header, step progress chip, 9-step pill navigator, the Visit details card (read-only auditor ID + date, and the first multi-choice question), and the fixed bottom Back / Save & exit / Next footer.
verdict: A clean, calm green-on-cream wizard that is functionally complete and reads well; it correctly opts into responsive gutters/content-max-width via useResponsiveLayout + getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, and the footer respects gesture-nav insets. The main weaknesses are Android-specific: the whole screen renders fixed phone-sized typography (it never applies TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE and bypasses the shared ScaledText primitives), and it makes no large-screen layout adaptation (single centered column, no list-detail or rail), so on a tablet it reads as a scaled-up phone form.

improvements.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx — all text nodes (e.g. StepHeader title fontSize={30} line 614, Card title fontSize={22} line 1094, QuestionCard label fontSize={16} line 1169, Step pill fontSize={11} line 605)
improvements.suggestion: Font sizes are hard-coded literals and never multiplied by TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE (1.3) even though layout.isTablet is available from useResponsiveLayout(). The design system explicitly intends tablet body text to render ~1.3x larger for legibility (lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts:792). On this Android tablet the title and option labels read small for the canvas. Derive sizes from layout (e.g. multiply by the tablet base scale when layout.isTablet) instead of fixed numbers.
improvements.evidence: core.md lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts:792 (TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE = 1.3) vs audit-placeId-step.md:614,1094,1169,605 fixed fontSize; image shows phone-scale type on a tablet width

improvements.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:22-23 (imports Text/Paragraph from tamagui and the static `designSystem`)
improvements.suggestion: Every label uses tamagui's raw Text/Paragraph instead of the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph, so explicit numeric fontSize is not multiplied by the auditor's stored fontScale preference (components/ui/ScaledText.tsx:2295-2321). The pack's `design_system_components_used: (none)` confirms no shared primitives are used. Swap to ScaledText/ScaledParagraph (as other CORE components do, e.g. ScreenHeader.tsx) so the accessibility text-size slider affects this field-heavy audit form.

The screen reads the static light-only `designSystem` constant rather than `useDesignSystem()`, so it will not re-render on theme or dyslexic-font preference changes (lib/design-system.ts:453-510). Not visible in this light capture, but it means dark mode / dyslexic font won't apply to the audit wizard. Switch to useDesignSystem() and pass colors down, consistent with the rest of the app.
improvements.evidence: audit-placeId-step.md:23 vs core.md lib/design-system.ts:477-510 (getDesignSystem honors theme + dyslexicFont)

improvements.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx StepHeader pill row (lines 669-703) and single-column ContextStep (lines 717-808)
improvements.suggestion: On the tablet canvas the screen is a single centered form column with a wrapping row of 9 step pills. No list-detail, multi-column, or persistent step-rail adaptation is used despite the extra width. A vertical step rail / sidebar (or a 2-column card layout for short read-only fields like Auditor ID + Audit date) would use the tablet space better than stacking and wrapping. Form content is intentionally width-constrained (formMaxWidth), so keep the inputs narrow but consider relocating step navigation to a rail.
improvements.evidence: image (wide single column, pills wrap to two rows); core.md lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts supportRailWidth tokens exist but are unused here

improvements.suggestion: Option rows are built from a pressable XStack with token padding (py="$3") rather than the responsive formOptionHeight (48-52dp on tablet, lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts). The rendered single-line rows look comfortable and likely clear 48dp, but they don't key off layout.formOptionHeight, so they don't grow on larger tablets. Consider applying a minHeight from layout.formOptionHeight to guarantee the Android 48dp target across tablet tiers.

tamagui_notes: Screen hand-rolls all styling inline from the static `designSystem` object and a local SurveyPalette (audit-placeId-step.md:1787-1805) instead of using any shared ui/* primitive — the pack's `design_system_components_used: (none)` line confirms this; the consequence is the missing ScaledText/useDesignSystem behaviors flagged above.
SelectionButton intentionally avoids tamagui's Button so labels can wrap (comment at audit-placeId-step.md:1284-1286) — a justified deviation, not a bug.
Footer Next button color comes from nextTone.stepText which resolves to designSystem.colors.primary (#10231F) with white text — primaryForeground on primary is high-contrast (visible in image).
platform_notes: Android nav bar is hidden app-wide via useHiddenAndroidNavBar (core.md lib/system-bars.ts:1069); the footer pads paddingBottom={bottomInset + 12} (audit-placeId-step.md:1680) so primary actions clear gesture insets — good.

Native stack header uses headerTitleAlign 'left' on Android (useYeeStackHeaderOptions.ts:1998-1999), matching Material left-aligned titles; the visible 'audit/[placeId]' title is the raw route name because this capture renders the default Stack screen title rather than the YeeStackHeaderTitle (the route param wasn't resolved to a label in the screenshot harness).
No iOS-ported chevrons in the footer — Back uses an arrow-left Feather icon (components/icons.tsx) which is platform-neutral; acceptable on Android.
not_assessable: Dark-theme and dyslexic-font rendering of this screen (only a light capture provided; the static designSystem concern is inferred from code, not seen).
Exact dp of the option-row tap targets and exact WCAG contrast ratios (estimated only).
Runtime states not shown: loading spinner, error NoticeCard, the condition follow-up sub-card, and the step-2..9 layouts.
Whether the wrapped 9-pill navigator overflows or scrolls on narrower tablet widths than this capture.
score_rationale: Solid and shippable with minor polish: layout is responsive at the container level, insets are handled, and the visual design is clean and on-brand. It loses points for two real, code-confirmed gaps that matter on a tablet — fixed phone-sized typography that never applies TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE and bypasses the shared ScaledText accessibility primitives — plus the absence of any genuine large-screen layout adaptation. None are broken or off-platform, so this sits at the top of the 7-8 band.
